claims.source: Kevin Day, public documentary and broadcast interviews, 2018-2019; no primary record located as of Aug 2026
claims.text: Recording media documenting the Princeton radar tracks were removed by personnel who did not identify themselves within roughly 48 hours of the intercept. Reasoning: the account is consistent across Day's public interviews and with Gary Voorhis's independent account of being ordered to reformat/hand over data, and it is compatible with - not contradicted by - Fravor's statement that no tapes were taken from his aircrew, since the two men describe collection aimed at different platforms. It remains inference until a visit log, message, or FOIA release names the personnel.

conflicts: Fravor testified under his own name that 'tapes were never taken.' Day says media were taken from Princeton. The reconciliation is platform-specific collection, but the conflict is real and should be presented, not smoothed.

label: Kevin Day
narrative: Day was the Senior Chief Operations Specialist running the air picture in USS Princeton's combat information center during the two weeks of contacts that culminated in the 14 November 2004 intercept. His role is the load-bearing one for the radar side of the case: the Princeton's SPY-1B, freshly upgraded, was the sensor that established the objects were descending from above 80,000 feet, that they were numerous, and that they were not tracks the Aegis library recognised. Fravor's own sworn statement to House Oversight corroborates the substance of Day's picture - that Princeton 'had been observing these objects on their Aegis combat system for the previous 2 weeks' descending 'from above 80,000ft ... rapidly down to 20,000ft.' Day has said publicly in documentary and broadcast interviews that within a day or two of the intercept, personnel who did not identify themselves arrived aboard Princeton and removed recording media, and that he was told to stop discussing it. That confiscation account is the pivot of the whole coverup strand for this incident and it has not yet been anchored to a primary record - no FOIA release, no visit log, no message traffic identifying the personnel or the authority under which they acted has surfaced. It is recorded here as a tier-2 attributed account with the primary-record gap stated plainly, because a fabricated citation would destroy exactly the claim that most needs to survive audit.
